$comment: Rule catalog — literature comparison, citations, novelty. Standard 14.

rules.title: Results are compared against the literature
rules.description: Before promotion to proved rank, a claim carries a record of what was searched and what was found — including a negative result and where it looked.
rules.rationale: A recorded negative search is evidence with limits; an absent one is indistinguishable from not having looked.
rules.remediation: Record the search as citation-type evidence: databases, terms, date, and outcome. The three useful outcomes are known, new, or a special case of something known.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that a comparison was recorded. Whether the search was competent — whether it used the terms the field actually uses — is review.

rules.title: External references carry resolvable identifiers
rules.description: Every external: identifier used in a Depends or Assumptions field is defined in the ledger's References section, and any DOI or arXiv identifier there is well-formed.
rules.rationale: A reference nobody can resolve is a dependency the project cannot identify.
rules.remediation: Add the reference with authors, title, year, venue, and a DOI or arXiv identifier where one exists.
rules.$assuranceNote: Syntactic and offline. A well-formed identifier for a paper that does not exist passes. This repository makes no network calls during an audit and would not gain the right to merely because it would be convenient, so the rule catches malformed references and typos, and catches nothing of the failure Standard 14 is actually about.

rules.title: Citations and known results are never fabricated
rules.description: A cited work does not exist, or an asserted known result is not in the literature.
rules.rationale: The failure mode is not deliberate invention. It is an agent generating a reference that fits the shape of the argument, with plausible authors, a plausible venue, a well-formed identifier, and no underlying paper — and a human reading past it because it looks exactly like the citations around it.
rules.remediation: Open every cited work and confirm it exists. Remove any reference that cannot be resolved to a real document.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector. Establishing existence requires resolving the reference against the world, which an offline checker cannot do. Established by a person opening the paper, recorded as an attestation.

rules.title: Novelty is never claimed without checking prior work
rules.description: A claim asserts novelty and carries no citation-type evidence recording a prior-work search.
rules.rationale: Novelty matters when the claim is being published, when priority is asserted, or when the project's value depends on the result being new — and in exactly those cases the cost of being wrong is highest.
rules.remediation: Record the prior-work search as citation-type evidence, or drop the novelty claim.
rules.$assuranceNote: Matches novelty assertions in the claim's own text and checks for a recorded search. Novelty claimed in a paper draft rather than in the ledger is not seen, and the quality of the recorded search is not assessed.

rules.title: A citation never supports more than its source proves
rules.description: A real, resolvable reference is cited for a statement stronger than the one it establishes — an extra hypothesis dropped, a domain widened, a conclusion strengthened.
rules.rationale: More dangerous than fabrication precisely because every mechanical check passes: the paper exists, the identifier resolves, the authors are right, and the theorem is not the one being used.
rules.remediation: Record the cited result as the source states it. Where the citing work needs more, the gap is a proof obligation, not a citation.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector, and literature.resolvable-identifiers passing is not evidence against it. Established only by a person comparing the cited theorem against the use made of it.
